title: High-Capacity Generalized Hopfield Networks
abstract: Generalized Hopfield networks are introduced where memories and neurons are continuous variables that lie on a Riemannian manifold. We explicitly focus on symmetric spaces associated with the special unitary groups SU(d), and use both numerical and analytical (replica) techniques to demonstrate an almost order of magnitude enhancement in critical capacity over the vector networks starting with d=3 and further rapidly growing with d. To circumvent the non-linear geometric constraints, we use a Lie algebraic method [following V. Galitski, Phys. Rev. A 84, 012118 (2011)] to exactly describe the classical neural network in terms of linear algebra in an auxiliary Hilbert space. It is shown that in contrast to the traditional Hopfield networks, memory recall in SU(d) Hopfields corresponds to neuron alignment along a top eigenvector of a spiked matrix, which is less susceptible to random matrix crosstalk than other models with continuous neuron variables. Physical platforms to realize SU(d) Hopfields are briefly discussed and physical (in addition to algorithmic) recall mechanism is demonstrated, where memory recovery occurs naturally through generalized Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics. To illustrate SU(3) memory recall, we introduce a color (RGB) image encoding/decoding protocol and explicitly run image recovery on corrupted cues. Finally, we quantize the generalized Hopfields which are shown to reduce to Sachdev-Ye glassy type of models. Their many-body spectra generally feature two types of dark and memory bands, where the latter exhibits chaotic Wigner-Dyson level statistics that hides Hebbian data.
summary: This paper generalizes Hopfield networks by placing neurons on the $	ext{SU}(d)$ manifold ($	ext{CP}^{d-1}$), achieving a significant boost in memory capacity over standard models. It employs advanced techniques, including Lie algebra and replica analysis, to show that recall is governed by alignment along top eigenvectors. The results are validated using physical dynamics (LLG) and suggest connections to quantum glassy systems.
main_problem: To develop generalized Hopfield networks using continuous variables on Riemannian manifolds to significantly enhance memory storage capacity beyond traditional vector models.
main_result: The use of $	ext{SU}(d)$ symmetry leads to a strong, order-of-magnitude enhancement in critical capacity ($\alpha_c$) compared to standard spherical networks. Furthermore, physical dynamics (LLG) successfully reproduce these high capacities.
method: The analysis combines replica techniques with Lie algebraic methods to linearize the geometric constraints of the manifold. Retrieval is analyzed using energy minimization principles derived from generalized Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is a Hopfield network where neurons and memories reside on symmetric spaces, specifically $	ext{SU}(d)$ associated with the manifold $	ext{CP}^{d-1}$. The system's energy functional governs memory storage and retrieval.
key_observables: Critical capacity ($\alpha_c$), Memory Overlap ($O_\mu$), and the success rate of image recovery during dynamics.
important_parameters: The dimension $d$ of the special unitary group, which dictates the manifold structure; the load parameter $\alpha$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the non-linear geometry onto an auxiliary Hilbert space using Lie algebra techniques. The LLG dynamics are assumed to govern physical recall.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate image encoding/decoding protocols for SU(3) and show capacity scans demonstrating high $\alpha_c$ values, alongside visualizations of winner-takes-it-all behavior during retrieval.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the generalized network on Riemannian manifolds, derives the energy functional using Lie algebra, analyzes the enhanced capacity via replica methods, demonstrates physical recall using LLG dynamics (including image examples), and concludes by quantizing the system to relate it to Sachdev-Ye glassy models.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from quantum information (SU(d) representations, complex structures) with condensed matter physics (spin glasses, disordered systems) via neural network modeling. The connection between geometric constraints and enhanced capacity is highly relevant for understanding physical implementations of memory storage.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Examples of memories stored for the SU(3) image- recall demonstration. (a) A fragment of a color photo (we have chosen one of the earliest known color photographs by Prokudin-Gorsky taken in 1909 using RGB filters [14]). The image is compressed into a 180 × 180 = 32400-pixel matrix which is flattened into a memory vector, ξµ=0 i , where i runs over 32400 components. Each pixel is a neuron which is en- coded as a qutrit on CP 2 through the color-to-qutrit map of Eq. (16). (b),(c) Two Haar-random qutrit memories, shown decoded back to RGB.

FIG. 2. Image recall from the corrupted cue using the top eigenvector update procedure for the SU(3) neural network. The progression illustrates the “restoration” of the image as a function of “time,” measured in the fraction of a single sweep (32400 individual neuron updates). For this ultra-low load of the network (100 Haar random memories and the target image) the near perfect restoration is achieved within a single sweep and then settles to a 100% match.

FIG. 3. Numerical simulations of the SU(d) recall for d = 2, 3, and 4 for P Haar random memories on CP d−1. Mean retrieval overlap ¯m0 = d 2(d−1) O0 with Oµ defined in Eq. (11) is plotted as a function of the network load. The dashed lines mark the threshold ¯mth = 1/2. We observe a sharp deterioration of the image recovery process and estimate the critical capacity, αc from this behavior. It shows an order of magnitude enhancement starting with d = 3.

FIG. 4. (a) Replica-symmetric retrieval overlap ¯m = m/L versus load α for the d = 3 (CP 2, qutrit) network, from the T = 0 self-consistent equations (32) averaged over ∼104 samples of the matrix field ˆK. The stable (solid) and unstable (dashed) branches merge at the critical load that defines αc ≃0.62. (b) Critical capacity αc as a function of the qudit dimension d, obtained from the T = 0 replica-symmetric equations (32). The values αc ≃0.05, 0.62, 2.5, 6.6, 13.6, 24.6, 40.3 for d = 2, . . . , 8 rise steeply, exceeding unity for d ≥4 and far above the binary value 0.138.

FIG. 5. Density of states of the quantum XY Hopfield model in the two-magnon sector as a function of the transverse field. The parameters are N = 160 and P = 16, corresponding to a load of 10%. The magnetic field is taken to be hi = Wui, where the random variables ui are drawn uniformly from the interval [−1, 1]. In the absence of a magnetic field, a flat (dark) band is observed, originating from the zero modes of the Hebb matrix. As the field strength increases, the dark band broadens and eventually merges with the memory band.
